body_long:
Gencom, the American investment firm founded by Karim Alibhai, announced on 3 November 2026 that it has acquired Rosewood London, the 308-key hotel at 252 High Holborn. La Revue des Hôtels describes it as Gencom's first luxury hotel acquisition in Europe.

## The deal

HSBC and Santander provide a £225 million senior debt package, about €269.6 million. HVS Hodges Ward Elliott represented the seller, who has not been named, and the price has not been disclosed. Gencom says it will carry out a focused capital expenditure plan; no budget or timetable has been published.

Rosewood London becomes Gencom's second Rosewood property, after Rosewood Bermuda, acquired in 2017. The firm has also bought the Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park, and announced the InterContinental Miami on 30 October.

Alessandro Colantonio, Gencom's chief investment officer, describes the hotel as an emblematic and irreplaceable asset. Radha Arora, president of Rosewood Hotel Group, says he is pleased to continue the relationship with Gencom. No change of operator has been announced, and the hotel remained bookable on 4 November.

## The hotel

The Edwardian building dates from 1912 and is Grade II listed. Tony Chi Studios led its transformation between 2011 and 2014, and it took the Rosewood name in October 2013. It counts 264 rooms and 44 suites, including seven "Houses" of up to 185 square metres; the Manor House Suite has its own street entrance.

Food and drink carry much of its reputation: the Holborn Dining Room and Scarfes Bar, both designed by Martin Brudnizki, a Gin Bar with more than 300 gins, the Mirror Room and the Pie Room. There is also a Sense spa and eleven event spaces.

On 4 November, La Revue des Hôtels found an Executive Twin at £968 for the night of 1 December, and £576 non-refundable for a night in January.

Rosewood now has two London addresses: The Chancery Rosewood, in the former US embassy in Mayfair, opened in September 2025.

## The signal

London's trophy hotels still attract foreign capital, and the brand stays when the owner changes. For the team on High Holborn, the question now is the scale and pace of the new owner's reinvestment, at a time when The Chancery Rosewood raises the bar within the same brand.
summary: Gencom has acquired the 308-key Rosewood London on High Holborn, financed by £225 million of senior debt from HSBC and Santander. Price undisclosed; Rosewood stays in place.
